subject.title: message_tool_only: one-shot delivery reminder loses to recency over long tool chains, turns end in withheld finals

question: For long `message_tool_only` turns that end with a substantive plain final, should OpenClaw add periodic delivery-contract refresh, one-shot withheld-final recovery, or both?
rationale: Current source proves the one-time hint and warning-only suppression path, but choosing when to re-prompt or retry affects context size, duplicate-delivery risk, and the documented privacy contract.

options.title: Combine refresh and recovery
options.body: Add a fixed-size reminder after bounded tool activity and a one-shot recovery path for substantive private finals, coordinated with the open stranded-final recovery work.

options.title: Recovery only
options.body: Use the existing private-final warning point to repair missed finals after the model fails, without adding prompt traffic during long tool chains.

options.title: Reminder only
options.body: Refresh the delivery instruction during long turns but leave actual withheld-final retry or diagnostics to separate recovery work.

recommendation.title: Combine refresh and recovery
recommendation.body: Add a fixed-size reminder after bounded tool activity and a one-shot recovery path for substantive private finals, coordinated with the open stranded-final recovery work.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current history signal for the per-turn delivery contract that would need to be refreshed or reshaped.
